subject: Availability tiers, escalation coverage and commercial options
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex@clearpathanalytics.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Availability tiers / support ask

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demos last week. Our execs want a short paper that outlines: uptime tiers you offer, what the commercial impact is (credits / refunds), and what 24/7 escalation looks like for mission-critical workflows. ClearPath is leaning toward a committed model if the uptime and on-call response times are strong.

Can you send a single-page matrix that includes pricing delta for Premium Support (24/7 on-call + dedicated escalation engineer) and any discount thresholds tied to term/commit? Also, is there a standard credit formula for downtime (hours vs. minutes)?

We'd like to have something to discuss internally by Thursday EOD.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Platform Engineering
ClearPath Analytics

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@clearpathanalytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-11T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Availability tiers / support ask

Alex —

Appreciate the clear outline. Attached is a concise matrix (PDF) and a short commercial summary below. High-level options we typically propose:

Tier A — Standard (included)
- Target availability: 99.5%
- Response: business-hours support (Mon-Fri 9–6 PDT), P1 initial response SLA 4 hours
- Credits: pro-rated service credit computed as percentage of monthly bill after 24 cumulative minutes below target per month
- Pricing: included with hosted usage (no separate fee)

Tier B — Business+
- Target availability: 99.9%
- Response: extended hours (M-F 7–11 PDT + on-call overlap), P1 SLA 60 minutes
- Credits: 10% monthly credit if uptime falls below 99.9% (scaled)
- Premium Support add-on: $8,000/month (or a 10% surcharge on committed spend) for prioritized routing and a designated TAM during business hours

Tier C — Mission (Premium)
- Target availability: 99.95%
- Response: 24/7 on-call with escalation engineer, P1 SLA 15 minutes, P2 SLA 2 hours
- Credits: 25% monthly credit if uptime < 99.95% (detailed schedule in matrix)
- Premium Support + Escalation Engineer: $16,000/month (flat) OR 20% discount on unit usage with an annual committed spend >= $1,200,000

Discount mechanics we can offer:
- 12-month commit: up to 10% off list depending on spend band
- 24-month commit: up to 20% off + waived onboarding fee
- Volume bands (committed monthly spend) drive deeper discounts and can be combined with Premium Support pricing.

Credit calculation (standard):
- Credits calculated as percentage of monthly invoice for the affected service, applied to the following billing cycle. Downtime measured in the smallest resolution we collect (seconds) and rounded to minutes for credit bands. We can show a worked example in the MSA.

I've attached the PDF and a draft MSA for redlines. If you want, Neha can run through the precise discount bands and Laura can put together a formal commercial term sheet.

Best,
Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: ClearPath_Redwood_Support_Matrix.pdf, draft_msa_redwood_v1.docx

From: Alex Morgan <alex@clearpathanalytics.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearpathanalytics.com
Date: 2026-06-12T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Availability tiers / support ask

Rishi —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple of follow-ups from our side:
1) For Tier C, can you confirm that the 15-minute P1 SLA includes acknowledgement and start of remediation (not full resolution)? We need clarity on "response" vs "resolution\."
2) Is the 25% credit maximum per month or per incident? Our procurement team prefers a per-incident ladder that scales with duration.
3) On discounts: the 20% for $1.2M/yr is attractive. Would you consider 22.5% if we sign a 36-month commitment and guarantee a minimum committed spend of $4M?

Also, procurement asked to see any carve-outs in the credit policy (force majeure / scheduled maintenance windows).

If you can answer inline we can escalate to execs tomorrow.

Alex

> Alex —
> 
> Appreciate the clear outline. Attached is a concise matrix (PDF) and a short commercial summary below. High-level options we typically propose...

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@clearpathanalytics.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-13T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Availability tiers / support ask — commercial clarifications

Alex / team —

Quick answers to your bullets and a commercial counter-proposal:  
1) "Response" vs "Resolution" — correct, our P1 SLA is defined as "initial response and engagement" (acknowledge + begin mitigation). We will make that definition explicit in the MSA.

2) Credit model — our default is a monthly aggregate credit (caps and ladders in the matrix). That said, for Enterprise customers on Mission tier we will accept a per-incident ladder (example: 15–60 min = 5% credit, 60–180 min = 15% credit, >180 min = 40% credit) with a per-incident cap equal to the monthly credit cap. We can include both metrics in the SLO schedule.

3) Discount flexibility — we can move on the 36-month ask. Proposed counter: 36-month commitment with minimum $4.0M total spend yields a 23% discount on unit pricing + waived onboarding and migration support fees. We need to preserve the Premium Support flat fee or convert it to a blended percent-of-spend model (we propose 15% of committed monthly spend as an alternative).

Carve-outs: scheduled maintenance windows (we publish a quarterly maintenance calendar) and force majeure are standard carve-outs. We will define maintenance windows as planned disruptions announced at least 72 hours in advance; emergency maintenance to maintain security will be accounted for separately and communicated.

If that works, Laura can draft the final commercial sheet and Stephanie will prepare an SLA schedule for the MSA.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@clearpathanalytics.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Availability tiers / support ask — legal / SLA notes

Alex:

Couple of legal / SLA clarifications we should flag now (so procurement doesn't get surprised):
- Credit calculation: credits are calculated as a percentage of the affected service's monthly invoice and are applied to the following invoice. We typically cap total credits at 100% of the affected service charges for the month.
- Measurement: uptime is measured at the service ingress point. We will include the precise metric and measurement windows in the SLO attachment.
- Remedies: credits are the exclusive monetary remedy; customers may terminate for material repeated SLA breaches (e.g., two consecutive months below Tier C target) — termination for convenience is not affected.
- Exceptions: security incidents tied to customer-managed keys or customer network misconfiguration are excluded.
- Escalation scope: our Mission tier includes a named escalation engineer and 24/7 rota; however, for dedicated on-prem deployments we may require on-prem runbook cooperation and periodic tabletop exercises to meet the 15-minute engagement expectation.

We'll incorporate the per-incident ladder Neha proposed and draft the redline for the MSA. If ClearPath is comfortable, we can issue a commercial term sheet tomorrow for signature and route the MSA for redlines simultaneously.

Regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

---
Alex — please let us know if the 23%/36-month counter is acceptable and whether procurement wants the support fee as flat or percent-of-spend. We can produce two term sheets (flat fee vs blended) so execs can choose quickly.

From: Alex Morgan <alex@clearpathanalytics.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearpathanalytics.com
Date: 2026-06-15T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Availability tiers / support ask — commercial clarifications

Team —

Appreciate the level of detail. ClearPath is comfortable with the 36-month / $4M min and the 23% discount. We prefer the flat support fee for predictability; please include the flat $16,000/month option in the term sheet. Procurement will review the per-incident ladder and carve-outs; the acknowledgement vs resolution wording is acceptable as long as it is explicit in the MSA.

Next steps: issue two term-sheet PDFs (one with flat fee, one blended) and send the MSA redline to procurement. If everything looks good we will aim to sign by end of month.

Regards,
Alex Morgan
Head of Platform Engineering
ClearPath Analytics
